_comment: Deliberate exceptions to the extension-term guard (scripts/check-extension-terms.ts): project-owned or mirrored IRIs that are referenced without a definition in any ontology, for a documented reason. Keep this list short: the normal fix is to define the term or repoint the reference. Every entry needs a reason that says why the term cannot simply be defined.

allow.reason: Upstream inconsistency, mirrored faithfully: the GS1 Rail context (https://gs1-epcis-reg.org/rail/rail-context.jsonld) declares this term while the GS1 Rail vocabulary (gs1RailVoc, v1.6) does not define it. rail: is an upstream namespace (GS1 AISBL / GS1 Switzerland); minting into it is not ours to do. Re-check with `pnpm sync:rail`.
Same upstream context-vs-vocabulary gap as rail:manufacturer: the upstream context defines the term, the vocabulary does not. Re-check with `pnpm sync:rail`.
Same upstream context-vs-vocabulary gap as rail:manufacturer: the upstream context defines the term, the vocabulary does not. Re-check with `pnpm sync:rail`.

Defined by GS1 Rail v1.6 and dropped in v2.6 (2026-11-06 sync). Referenced only by the served, frozen v1.6 context extensions/upstream/gs1-rail/context/rail-context.jsonld, which stored documents expand against and which must not be redefined.
